analysis.title: Macro Volatility Digest: Tech Rout, Muted Vol: Bullish Positioning Unwinds
key_insights: Equities sold off last week on disappointing Tech earnings, but implied vols were muted across asset classes. The VIX ended the week unchanged at about 19.5% (75th percentile over the past year).
Rates volatility fell modestly after the Fed meeting. The OIS market prices about a 75% probability of a hike at the next meeting.
TLT options skew fell from near a 1-year high to near a 1-year low on stronger demand for upside calls. More investors are positioning for long-end yields to fall on a more uncertain macro outlook.
The 1M rolling correlation between the SPX and the 10Y Treasury yield rose from -70% to +40% as investor focus shifted from inflation to growth risk.
Oil volatility eased slightly ahead of the US midterm elections despite ongoing Middle East turmoil that has kept oil prices elevated. The OVX fell 1.5 vol pts to 58% (64th percentile).
Gold was the only asset class to see implied vol rise last week. GLD 1M implied vol rose 1.6 pts to 23% (49th percentile) as gold fell to a 1-year low.
On Friday the SPX fell 1.8% and QQQ fell 3.5%, but SPX 1M fixed-strike vols rose only 0.6 pt. SPX put skew and put convexity both fell as investors monetized existing hedges.
Hedging demand in SPX options had risen over prior weeks, which helped cap the VIX move last week.
9 of 11 S&P sectors were up on the week, led by Healthcare +3%, against Comm Services down 8.5%. The sector rotation is another reason index vol was muted.
Average single-stock vol (VIXEQ) rose 0.4 pt week over week with earnings more than halfway complete.
SPX 1M skew (25-delta ratio) remains in the 80th percentile high.

Single-stock call demand dropped sharply and hedging demand rose. The share of S&P top 100 stocks with inverted call skew, which signals extreme bullish sentiment, fell from a high of 44% in early October to 10%.
Retail put buying in mega-cap Tech hit a YTD high last week at 34% of opening trades, against an average of 24%.

sector_views.rationale: Healthcare rose 3% on the week and led 9 of 11 S&P sectors higher.
Comm Services fell 8.5% on the week, the weakest sector, on disappointing Tech earnings.

earnings_insights: Disappointing Tech earnings drove last week's equity sell-off. Earnings season is more than halfway complete as of the report date.

tension_points.bull_case: Muted vol and monetized hedges show little panic, and 9 of 11 sectors rose on the week, so rotation is absorbing the Tech sell-off.
tension_points.bear_case: SPX skew stays in the 80th percentile, hedging demand and mega-cap Tech put buying are at a YTD high, and the stock-bond correlation flip points to growth risk.
